lines.text: Work however not only makes the body tired, and is
physically fatiguing, but it can also consume our inner
strength. Those who are engaged in work which with its
plans and prospects claims their whole attention, are always
in danger of forgetting their souls through their absorption
in such work. For such people the time for recollection, and
self-examination in the presence of God, for realizing the
primordial necessity of God's blessing on their work, becomes
ever shorter and in the end threatens to vanish altogether.
We say of course that "so and so is utterly taken up with his
work" and more often than not we do not realize what a
condemnation this implies. A man of this kind must lose the
whole basis and poise of his life if he has the misfortune to
meet with failure, for it was only his work which gave his
life its support; and if such a one becomes incapable of work,
then he loses the content of his life completely, for it was only
his work which gave his life its content and meaning. Thus
it appears that work can be not only a blessing but also a
curse, and can, as it were, eat up and dissipate a man's life.
We detect in the people of our acquaintance whether they
are merely workers (rather like working animals) as opposed
to human beings, for such people are incapable of taking
part in a genuine community life, and sharing the joys and
sorrows of others.
II
Now it is just these things of which Sunday reminds us.
The words of Jesus are a summons to all those who are
weary and heavy laden. Sunday invites these tired and
burdened souls to become refreshed and renewed. But
Sunday can pour its healing balm only on those who realize
their need. Woe to them it,
, in their preoccupation with toil,
they forget their soul's need! In fact, Sunday is not intended
to be simply a superficial day of rest for those who feel weary
and run down by the labours of the week, but according to
its true meaning and purpose it is a day of rest and refresh-
